summary:
SIMULATION: VARIANT 5 ("LES DEUX") TRADED IN WHOLE CONTRACTS, BY CAPITAL
Folder: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-snt-2b-adam-cieniewicz/4246b01c-1857-5934-aed2-b3eb85d88a07/scratchpad/audit/simulation/

Main file: results.csv, with 152 rows. Each row is one combination of universe × capital × notional mode × rebalancing frequency × period. Nothing under /home/user/snt-2b-adam-cieniewicz was modified.

All returns are in excess of T-bill unless stated, with capital held fixed and P&L expressed as a % of that capital. CAGR and maxDD compound daily excess returns.

STEP 1 — NOTIONAL PER CONTRACT THROUGH TIME (what I did)

Why the back-adjusted prices could not be used:
- The dataset's "back-adjusted" prices are RATIO-adjusted. P_t/P_today is the excess-return index, not the price level.
- On 2000-01-03 the file shows: NG 924 against an actual price of about 2.3; wheat 9,922 c/bu against 292; corn 2,192 against 232; coffee 2,200 against 121.
- So notional_today × P_t/P_today, and the return-index rebuild (which is the same thing), are off by factors of 3 to 300 for any commodity with roll yield. I used neither for commodities.

Actual price levels, in dataset units:
- **72 markets:** Carver's pysystemtrade multiple_prices PRICE column (the contract actually held).
  - Most files are the local copy in verify_trend_C/data.
  - I fetched GASOIL from raw GitHub, because the existing map pointed QS1 to GASOILINE, which is RBOB. I mapped XB1 to GASOILINE.
  - Units were converted with a power-of-10 factor.
- **2024-04 to 2026-07 (where pysystemtrade ends):** P_adj × a factor interpolated linearly from the pysystemtrade/P_adj ratio at its end down to 1 on 2026-07-10. That end ratio ranges from 0.64 (CL) to 1.44 (NG, CT).
- **Before each pysystemtrade series starts:** I chained on the ratio path, with these exceptions:
  - Bonds whose series starts late follow TY1's level path.
  - Coffee before 2007 uses the Yahoo KC=F front month.
  - MES1 before 2009 uses the geometric mean of the HSCEI and TAIEX paths.
  - JGS1, HC1 and TWT1 use local price indices.
  - MWE1 (spring wheat), CA1 (Euronext wheat) and IJ1 (rapeseed) use CBOT wheat or ICE canola paths, converted to EUR where needed.
  - QC1 Index, XP1, PT1, XM1 and IR4 stay on the ratio path. This is probably 15–50% too low in early years for those equity indices.
- **FX** comes from the actual prices of the FX futures.

Spot checks against known levels:

| Market | Date | Rebuilt level | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| ES | 2000-01-03 | 1467 | |
| CL | 2008-07-01 | 142.5 | |
| Gold | 2000 | 289.6 | |
| NG | 2000 | 2.33 | |
| Wheat | 2000 | 292 | |
| EURUSD | 2000 | 1.03 | |
| Bund | 2000 | 103 | |

Files: levels_check.csv, contracts_small.csv, contracts_liquid.csv.

Example notionals:

| Contract | 1999 | Today |
|---|---|---|
| Micro crude | $1.4k | $7.1k |
| 1OZ gold | $288 | $4,114 |
| MES | $6.2k | $38.1k |

**Two notional modes:**
- 'hist': actual historical notional, as the task asked.
- 'today': the 2026-07-10 notional and spread held constant through history. This is the forward-looking case for someone starting now. I quote it below unless I say otherwise.

**Micro contracts are assumed to have existed throughout.** In reality most date from 2019–2024.

ENGINE

- My engine.py reproduces trend.run_vol_targeted(..., forecast_regime) exactly: maximum position difference 0.0, Sharpe 1990+ 1.171.
- For subsets, it recomputes weights, IDM and the vol-target scale.
- Integer positions use Carver's AFTS strategy 8 buffering:
  - B = 0.1 × the position at forecast 10, in contracts.
  - lower = round(target − B), upper = round(target + B).
  - A trade happens only if the current position is outside [lower, upper].
  - The position is decided at the close on day t and held from t+1.
- The simulation starts on 1999-01-04. Evaluation windows are 2000-01 → 2026-07-10 and 2010-01 → 2026-07-10.

Costs:
- **(i)** The backtest's basis-point model applied to the integer trades, so results stay comparable.
- **(ii) "Realistic" — this is the net used for every Sharpe quoted below.** Per contract side: the fee from the cost audit / pysystemtrade (e.g. MES $0.62, micro FX $0.41, standard contracts about $2–3) plus the half-spread (pysystemtrade spread × multiplier × FX). For 25 micros with no data I assumed a $1.0 fee and 1.5× the standard contract's half-spread in price units.
- **(iii)** The flat commission you asked for, reported separately: $1.0 per micro side, $2.5 per standard side.
- Rolls count as 2 sides × |n| × rolls per year (4 for equities, bonds, STIR and FX; 12 energy; 6 metals; 5 agriculture), and one spread order per roll of a non-zero position.

Universes:
- **(a) all84:** the smallest contract in every market.
- **strict66:** the 66 retail-accessible markets from the capital audit, all traded with their liquid contract. Small positions round to 0.
- **(b) subset ≥1c:** the capital audit's greedy round-robin set, re-run with variant 5. Markets are then dropped one at a time until every market has a median |position| (2023-07 → 2026-07) of at least 1 contract at today's notional. That check removed 1–3 markets per tier; for example, at 100k it dropped PE1, CL1 and ER4, leaving 14 markets.
- **subset ≥4c:** the same with Carver's 4-contract rule. File: subsets.csv.

REFERENCES (fractional, basis-point costs)

| Portfolio | Sharpe 2000–26 | Sharpe 2010–26 | CAGR excess 2000–26 | CAGR excess 2010–26 | Vol |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ideal 84-market variant 5 | 0.845 | 0.541 | 17.5% | 10.0% | 21.5% |
| strict66 | 0.714 | 0.391 | 14.3% | 6.5% | |

- Most of the 84-versus-66 gap comes from two thin markets: CUA1 (ethanol) and SCO1 (SGX iron ore).
- Since 2010 they contributed +1.57% and +1.33% of capital per year (gross).
- Adding just those two back to strict66 gives Sharpe 0.797 / 0.514.
- Their contribution is suspicious: ethanol is illiquid and block-traded, and iron ore data only starts in 2016.

RESULTS — today's notional, daily, net of realistic costs

Sharpe and CAGR are shown as 2000–26 / 2010–26. maxDD is for 2000–26. Commission is the flat rate, 2010–26.

Fee plus half-spread for subset ≥1c, as % of capital per year: 3.3 (50k), 3.3 (100k), 4.7 (250k), 3.8 (500k), 3.3 (1M), 2.8 (2M), 2.5 (5M).

What this shows:
1. **For subsets, rounding is not the problem.** Correlation with their own fractional version is at least 0.993, and tracking error is 0.4–2.2% a year. Their weakness is lost diversification: own fractional Sharpe since 2000 is 0.47 (11 markets), 0.55 (14), 0.67 (24) and about 0.70 (32+), against 0.845 for all 84. Carver's 4-contract rule is worse than the 1-contract rule below 2M.
2. **Trading the whole accessible universe and letting small positions round to 0 is a valid alternative.**
   - Realised volatility falls well below target: 8.5% at 50k, 11% at 100k, 16% at 250k, 19% at 500k.
   - 89% / 81% / 65% / 50% / 33% / 20% / 9% of market-days with a non-zero target end up held at 0 contracts at 50k / 100k / 250k / 500k / 1M / 2M / 5M.
   - Tracking error against the ideal is 10–16% a year below 500k.
   - **The Sharpes here are dominated by noise.** Changing the minimum buffer from 0 to 1 contract moves strict66's 2010–26 Sharpe at 100k from 0.23 to 0.58, and at 1M from 0.46 to 0.64 (buffer_sensitivity.csv).
   - The standard error of the gap against fractional is about 0.2–0.3 Sharpe. Do not read 0.80 at 250k as a real improvement.
3. **Historical notional gives lower net Sharpe for small accounts.** For example, subset ≥1c at 100k is 0.50 (hist) versus 0.57 (today). In the past contracts were smaller, so more of them were needed and more per-contract fees paid.
4. **Weekly rebalancing**, subset ≥1c:

| Capital | Daily Sharpe (2000–26 / 2010–26) | Weekly Sharpe | Daily orders/yr | Weekly orders/yr | Daily commission | Weekly commission |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100k | 0.57 / 0.41 | 0.50 / 0.335 | 750 | 420 | 2.71% | 2.44% |
| 250k | 0.65 / 0.37 | 0.60 / 0.32 | 1,470 | 730 | 2.35% | 2.13% |

   - Weekly roughly halves the number of tickets, but barely reduces contracts traded or commission, because rolls are unchanged.
   - It costs about 0.05–0.07 of Sharpe. The fractional all84 weekly Sharpe is also lower: 0.785 against 0.845.
5. **Workload (2010–26, daily).**
   - strict66, orders per year:

| 50k | 100k | 250k | 500k | 1M | 2M | 5M | 20M |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 191 | 409 | 972 | 1,699 | 2,683 | 3,899 | 5,811 | 8,667 |

   - That is about 2–3 a day up to 100k, 4–6 a day at 250k, about 11 at 1M and about 23 at 5M. Beyond about 100–250k you need API automation.
   - Contract sides per year (trades plus rolls) for subset ≥1c:

| 50k | 100k | 250k | 500k | 1M | 2M | 5M |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 770 | 1,470 | 3,234 | 5,770 | 10,395 | 16,136 | 33,425 |

6. **all84 with micros and realistic costs** (not fully accessible) gets Sharpe 0.81–0.85 / 0.50–0.53 from 500k up, with tracking error under 5.4% a year from 500k and under 3% from 1M.

BOTTOM LINE FOR EXPECTED RETURN

| | Since 2010 | 2000–2026 |
|---|---|---|
| Sharpe | about 0.35–0.45 | about 0.57–0.72 at ≥100k |
| CAGR excess | about 5–8% | |
| Vol | about 21% | |
| maxDD | | −49% to −58% |

These are retail-accessible results, with realistic contract costs, before tax and before fixed data/software costs. The real-fund evidence (SG Trend, Sharpe 0.33) and the in-sample choice of variant 5 both argue for haircutting even these.

CAVEATS
- The micro-contract history is hypothetical.
- About 25 micro fee and spread figures are assumed.
- Some pysystemtrade spreads look conservative (Euribor at 0.0072 is wider than one tick; iron ore).
- Early levels for five unmapped markets are approximate.
- Positions are executed at the close with no extra slippage beyond the half-spread.
- Capital is held fixed (no compounding of contract counts).
- Margin and cash yield are not modelled; the excess returns are on top of T-bill.

claims.claim: The dataset's back-adjusted prices are ratio-adjusted (they behave as an excess-return index), so notional_today × P_t/P_today is unusable for commodities with roll yield. Actual levels were rebuilt from pysystemtrade multiple_prices.
claims.evidence: On 2000-01-03, P_adj is NG 924, wheat 9,922, corn 2,192 and coffee 2,200. The rebuilt actual levels are 2.33, 292, 232 and 121. Spot checks: ES 1467, CL 142.5 in July 2008, gold 289.6, EURUSD 1.03 (levels_check.csv).

claims.claim: For retail subsets, integer rounding with Carver buffering costs almost nothing. The loss against the backtest comes from lost diversification, not from rounding.
claims.evidence: Subsets have correlation of at least 0.993 with their own fractional version and tracking error of 0.4–2.2%/yr. Their own fractional Sharpe since 2000 is 0.47 (11 markets) to about 0.70 (32+ markets), against 0.845 for all 84.

claims.claim: A realistic retail-accessible implementation earned about Sharpe 0.35–0.45 since 2010 (CAGR excess about 5–8% at about 21% vol), and about 0.57–0.72 over 2000–2026 at ≥100k. This is before tax and fixed costs.
claims.evidence: summary_today_notional.csv rows for strict66 and subset ≥1c at 100k–20M.

claims.claim: The gap between the 84-market backtest and the 66 retail-accessible markets comes mostly from ethanol (CUA1) and SGX iron ore (SCO1), two thin or short-history markets.
claims.evidence: Fractional Sharpe since 2000 / since 2010: strict66 0.714/0.391; strict66 plus CUA1 and SCO1 0.797/0.514; all84 0.845/0.541. Since 2010, CUA1 contributed +1.57 and SCO1 +1.33 % of capital per year gross.

claims.claim: Below about 500k, trading the full accessible universe with rounding to zero has a much lower realised vol than the 20% target and a large tracking error. Its Sharpe is noise-dominated and highly sensitive to arbitrary buffer settings.
claims.evidence: strict66 vol is 8.5/11/15.7% at 50k/100k/250k, with tracking error against the ideal of 10–16%/yr. Raising the minimum buffer from 0 to 1 contract moves the 2010–26 Sharpe at 100k from 0.23 to 0.58 and at 1M from 0.46 to 0.64 (buffer_sensitivity.csv).

claims.claim: Carver's 4-contract rule gives worse results than the 1-contract rule below about 2M, because it leaves too few markets.
Commissions are a heavy drag for small accounts: about 2.7–2.9% of capital per year at 50–100k for a subset, and 3.3% including half-spreads.
claims.evidence: Subset ≥1c at 100k: 838 trade sides plus 632 roll sides per year, flat commission $2,705/yr = 2.7% of capital, fee plus half-spread 3.3% (2010–26, today notional).

claims.claim: Weekly rebalancing halves the number of orders but barely cuts commissions, and it costs about 0.05–0.07 of Sharpe.
claims.evidence: Subset ≥1c at 100k: 420 vs 750 orders/yr, 2.44% vs 2.71% commission, Sharpe 0.50 vs 0.57. At 250k: 730 vs 1,470 orders/yr, 2.13% vs 2.35%, Sharpe 0.60 vs 0.65.

claims.claim: The order workload calls for API automation above about 100–250k.
claims.evidence: strict66 orders per year (trades plus rolls): 409 at 100k, 972 at 250k, 2,683 at 1M, 5,811 at 5M — about 1.6, 3.9, 10.6 and 23 per trading day.

claims.claim: The capital audit's greedy subsets did not all pass an empirical check once re-run with adapted weights: 1–3 markets per tier fell below 1 (or 4) median contracts and were dropped.
claims.evidence: subsets.csv dropped_after_rerun column. For example, at 100k ≥1c it dropped PE1, CL1 and ER4; at 1M ≥1c it dropped SF1, SM1 Comdty and SI1.
